Committee: Ways and Means General Fund
Sponsor: Rich
Analyst: Vee Mosely
Date: 03/12/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 318 as introduced removes the requirement for the Alabama Onsite Wastewater Board (AOWB) to transfer unspent and unencumbered funds in the AOWB Fund that exceed 25 percent of the boards budget for the previous fiscal year. This provision could reduce potential receipts to the State General Fund by an undetermined amount based on (1) the unspent and unencumbered balance of the AOWB Fund at the end of each fiscal year and (2) the boards prior fiscal year budget. Over the past five fiscal years, the board made one transfer to the State General Fund in the amount of $52,257 in Fiscal Year 2018.
Further, this bill (1) increases maximum the administrative fine that may be levied by the board from $1,000 to $5,000 and (2) allows the board to recover interest and the costs of hearings for any licensee or other person who violates Chapter 21A of Title 34 or the boards rules. These provisions could increase receipts to the Alabama Onsite Wastewater Board Fund by an estimated maximum of $275,000 annually based on the historical number of cases brought to the board each year, the levy of the maximum administrative fines, and the actual historical costs of each hearing.
Steve Clouse, Chair
Ways and Means General Fund

Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Smitherman
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 03/31/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 158 as substituted and reported by the Committee on Judiciary requires the development, by October 1, 2023, of a Law Enforcement Officer Employment Database by the Alabama Peace Officers Standards and Training Commission (APOSTC) which would be used by law enforcement agencies to enter certain data regarding law enforcement officers and perform pre-employment checks on applicants. According to APOSTC, this will increase APOSTC's financial obligations by: (1) an estimated range of $2.9 - $3.9 million initially to develop the database, hire necessary additional personnel, and purchase computers and office equipment; and (2) an estimated $375,000 annually thereafter for maintenance of the database and employee salaries and expenses. Further, this bill could increase the administrative obligations of APOSTC to adopt rules to implement the provisions of this bill. This bill further provides for civil penalties of $1,000 and an additional $100 per day to be imposed upon law enforcement agencies found to be non-compliant in submitting data in accordance with the provisions of this bill which could increase receipts to the APOSTC Training Fund by an estimated minimum of $1,000 for each civil fine assessed and collected for non-compliance.
This bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, and local jails by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.
Jim Hill, Chair
Judiciary

Senate Bill 158 as substituted and reported by the Committee on Judiciary requires the development, by October 1, 2023, of a Law Enforcement Officer Employment Database by the Alabama Peace Officers Standards and Training Commission (APOSTC) which would, according to APOSTC, increase APOSTC's financial obligations by: (1) an estimated range of $2.9 to $3.9 million initially to develop the database, hire necessary additional personnel, and purchase computers and office equipment; and (2) an estimated $375,000 annually thereafter for maintenance of the database and employee salaries and expenses.
